study_strategy.look_here_first: Confirm Fraxinus with opposite branching + odd-pinnate leaves, then identify species with the samara wing/body relationship, leaflet number/texture, and twig leaf scar. Do not rely on leaf silhouette alone.

quick_key.if: small-to-medium limestone tree + 5–7 leaflets + glaucous/waxy lower surface + small samara with mostly terminal wing
riparian tree + 5–7(9) leaflets + shield-shaped scar + large samara whose wing runs well down body
3–5 leaflets + coarse sharp distal serration + occasional 3-winged fruits
xeric shrub/small tree + tiny leathery often nearly evergreen leaflets, commonly 3

study_strategy.priority_comparison: Fraxinus albicans vs Fraxinus pennsylvanica in Hays County — use samara, leaf scar, and lower-leaf wax; UT PRC notes co-occurrence and possible hybridization.
